filename: Buffering of Aerosol‐Cloud Adjustments by Coupling Between Radiative Susceptibility and Precipitation Efficiency.pdf
title: Buffering of Aerosol‐Cloud Adjustments by Coupling Between Radiative Susceptibility and Precipitation Efficiency
processes: Cloud albedo and shortwave radiative transfer
testbed_rationale: The CAM6 perturbed parameter ensemble dataset provides 262 configurations spanning 45 aerosol, convection, and cloud parameters with persistent public DOI access, which is directly suitable for benchmarking surrogate modeling, Gaussian process emulation, and parametric uncertainty quantification in Earth system models.
pain_points: Tight observational constraints on cloud microphysics (Nd) and macrophysics (LWP) fail to significantly reduce uncertainty in effective radiative forcing (ERFaci) due to physical buffering between precipitation efficiency and radiative saturation.
Lack of drop-size dependent entrainment-evaporation feedbacks parameterized in CAM6 and many standard GCM structures.
Difficulty in directly measuring in-cloud liquid water path (LWPc) globally without interference from overlying ice or low sun angles, requiring reliance on area-mean LWP.
Limited availability of comparable cloud-top droplet number concentration diagnostics across CMIP6 models.
extraction_notes: Gaussian Process emulators were constructed following Watson-Parris et al. (2021) and Lee et al. (2011) to sample 1,000,000 model parameter configurations from 262 PPE runs. Although ML is used as an emulator/UQ tool rather than an online parameterization, the study is funded partly by LEAP and provides an essential perturbed-parameter benchmark.
